mainTopic: Doubtful betrothal and theft among five people, a woman's report of deaths overseas, and whether a גט counts as a benefit for her
overview: The amud opens with a משנה about a man who betrothed one of five women, or stole from one of five people, and does not know which one. רבי טרפון says he may leave one payment for the group and walk away. רבי עקיבא says he must pay every one of them to be fully clear of sin. The גמרא notices that the משנה says קידש and גזל, and quotes a ברייתא in which רבי שמעון בן אלעזר places the argument in בעל and גזל instead. It answers that the משנה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: 'betrothed' means betrothed through relations, and each word was chosen to show how far one opinion goes. A new משנה then discusses a woman who returns from overseas and reports the order of her husband's and son's deaths. She is believed when her story keeps the status she left with. Otherwise we still take her words into account, so she does חליצה and not יבום. The גמרא asks whether a גט received for a woman counts as a benefit for her, both when she has a יבם and when the couple is fighting. It concludes from ריש לקיש and several folk sayings that a woman generally prefers to stay married, and the chapter ends with the הדרן.

steps.title: Betrothed one of five women: רבי טרפון's ruling
steps.stepSummary: A man betrothed one of five women and doesn't know which. Each woman claims him. רבי טרפון says he gives each a גט, leaves one כתובה among them, and leaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a man betrothed one of five women and doesn't know which one, and each says 'he betrothed me,' he gives a גט to every one of them. He leaves one כתובה payment for them to sort out, and he goes away. This is רבי טרפון's view.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens with a case of doubtful קידושין and gives רבי טרפון's ruling on how the man gets out of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every woman gets a גט, so none of them is left possibly married. But he only has to put down one כתובה, since he only owes it to one woman. The women must work out among themselves who gets it.

keyTerms.meaning: He betrothed (made קידושין)
A bill of divorce
The marriage contract payment owed to a wife when the marriage ends
He leaves it among them (for them to sort out)
He departs, removing himself from the matter

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the basic model of רבי טרפון: when you owe one person but don't know which, one payment left for the group is enough.

phrases.english: MISHNA: He betrothed one of five women,
and he does not know which one he betrothed,
and each one says: "He betrothed me"
he gives a bill of divorce to each and every one,
and he leaves a marriage contract payment among them, and departs,
these are the words of Rabbi Tarfon.

steps.triggerLanguage: קִידֵּשׁ אַחַת מֵחָמֵשׁ נָשִׁים, וְאֵין יוֹדֵעַ אֵי זוֹ קִידֵּשׁ
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In doubtful קידושין among five women, he gives each a גט and leaves a single כתובה among them (רבי טרפון).

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: he must give a גט and a כתובה to each woman
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא disagrees. Leaving one כתובה does not free the man from sin. He must give each woman both a גט and a full כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: That is not the way to get out of sin. He is not clear until he gives a גט and a כתובה to every single one of them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא argues on רבי טרפון about the betrothal case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that every woman needs a גט. The argument is only about money. רבי עקיבא worries that the real wife might never get the money she is owed, so to be fully clear of sin he must pay a כתובה to every woman.

keyTerms.meaning: This is not the way
Getting out of the grip of sin
Until he gives

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the core argument: is paying one share enough, or must a person go further to be sure he has not wronged anyone?

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: אֵין זוֹ דֶּרֶךְ
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says: This is not the way
to take someone out of the hands of sin,
phrases.notes: Literally 'out of the hands of sin.' He means this does not fully clear the man.

phrases.english: unless he gives a bill of divorce and a marriage contract payment
to each and every one.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: אֵין זוֹ דֶּרֶךְ מוֹצִיא מִידֵי עֲבֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי טרפון's ruling in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: To be free of sin, he must give each woman both a גט and a full כתובה (רבי עקיבא).

steps.title: Stole from one of five people: רבי טרפון's ruling
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives a parallel money case. Someone stole from one of five people and doesn't know which. רבי טרפון says he leaves the stolen amount among them and leaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a person stole from one of five people and doesn't know which, and each says 'he stole from me,' he leaves the stolen amount among them and goes away. This is רבי טרפון's view.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a second case of the same kind, this time about theft, and gives רבי טרפון's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The setup matches the betrothal case: one real victim, but nobody knows who. רבי טרפון is consistent. One payment, left for the group to divide, is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: He stole (robbed openly)
The stolen item or money
"He stole from me"

phrases.english: If he stole from one of five people
and does not know from which one he stole,
and each one says: "He stole from me"
he leaves the stolen item among them and departs,
these are the words of Rabbi Tarfon.

steps.triggerLanguage: גָּזַל אֶחָד מֵחֲמִשָּׁה וְאֵין יוֹדֵעַ מֵאֵיזֶה גָּזַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel case to step 1, now about theft instead of betrothal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In doubtful theft from one of five people, he leaves one payment among them (רבי טרפון).

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: the thief must pay each person
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא again disagrees. The thief is only free of sin if he pays every one of the five.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: That is not the way to get out of sin. He is not clear until he pays each and every one of them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא argues on רבי טרפון in the theft case, just as he did in the betrothal case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Same logic as before. Since the thief doesn't know whom he robbed, the only way to be sure the real victim is repaid is to pay all five.

keyTerms.meaning: That he pay
To each and every one

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה has two cases, betrothal and theft. In both, רבי טרפון says one payment left for the group is enough. רבי עקיבא says you must pay everyone to be fully clear of sin.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: אֵין זוֹ דֶּרֶךְ
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says: This is not the way
to take someone out of the hands of sin,
unless he pays each and every one.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: אֵין זוֹ דֶּרֶךְ מוֹצִיא מִידֵי עֲבֵירָה, עַד שֶׁיְּשַׁלֵּם לְכׇל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי טרפון's theft ruling in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In doubtful theft, he must repay each of the five (רבי עקיבא).

steps.title: The גמרא notices which words the משנה chose
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the משנה says קידש, not בעל, and גזל, not לקח. This suggests the argument is only about those specific cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says 'he betrothed.' It does not say 'he had relations' (בעל). It says 'he stole.' It does not say 'he bought' (לקח).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes an inference from the exact wording of the משנה. It is setting up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By choosing קידש and גזל, the משנה implies that רבי טרפון and רבי עקיבא argue about those cases. The related cases of בעל and לקח seem to follow a different rule that is not in dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches (the משנה says)
It does not teach
He had relations, here as the way of making קידושין
He bought

steps.confusionAlert: בעל here is not a sin. It means he made the קידושין through relations, one of the recognized ways of betrothal.

phrases.english: GEMARA: "He betrothed" is taught,
"He had relations" is not taught.
"He stole" is taught,
"He bought" is not taught.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the wording of the משנה's two cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's wording implies the dispute is specifically in קידש and גזל, not in בעל or לקח.

steps.title: Whose opinion is the משנה? It fits neither תנא קמא nor רבי שמעון בן אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: Based on that inference, the גמרא asks who wrote the משנה. It seems to match neither the תנא קמא nor רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is our משנה? It is not the תנא קמא's view, and it is not רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's view either!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a difficulty. The משנה's version of the argument does not match any known opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are known opinions about which cases רבי טרפון and רבי עקיבא really argued over. The משנה's picture, with the dispute in קידש and גזל, matches none of them. The גמרא will now prove this using a ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is our משנה?
The first, unnamed opinion in a teaching

phrases.english: Whose view is our Mishna?

phrases.aramaic: לָא תַּנָּא קַמָּא וְלָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר!
phrases.english: It is neither the first tanna nor Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar!
phrases.notes: The ברייתא coming up only quotes רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. The תנא קמא's view is worked out from his words in step 10.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַנִּי מַתְנִיתִין? לָא תַּנָּא קַמָּא וְלָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the inference from step 5 to question who the משנה's author is.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה puts the dispute in קידש and גזל, but the known opinions place the dispute elsewhere. So no known תנא matches it.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: in קידש everyone agrees
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says רבי טרפון and רבי עקיבא did not argue about the קידש case. Everyone agrees he leaves one כתובה among the women.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the ברייתא teaches: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says that רבי טרפון and רבי עקיבא did not argue about a man who betrothed one of five women and doesn't know which. Both agree he leaves the כתובה among them and goes away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up its claim that the משנה does not follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה shows רבי עקיבא arguing in the קידש case. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says even רבי עקיבא agrees there, so one כתובה is enough. That is a direct clash with the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא
They did not disagree

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
phrases.english: Rabbi Tarfon and Rabbi Akiva did not disagree
about one who betrothed one of five women
and does not know which one he betrothed,
that he leaves the marriage contract payment among them and departs.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up the claim in step 6 that the משנה does not match רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the משנה does not follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says there is no dispute in the קידש case

steps.title: According to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, the real dispute is about בעל
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. The argument was about a man who made the קידושין through relations (בעל). There, רבי טרפון says one כתובה is enough, and רבי עקיבא says he must pay each woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: So what did they argue about? About a man who betrothed through relations. רבי טרפון says he leaves the כתובה among them and goes away. רבי עקיבא says he is not clear until he pays every one of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes by saying where the real argument is. It moves the dispute from קידש to בעל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the reverse of what our משנה implied. The משנה argues about קידש and hints that בעל has a different rule. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says קידש is agreed and בעל is where they argue. So the משנה clearly does not follow him.

keyTerms.meaning: About what did they disagree?
About one who betrothed through relations

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה puts the רבי טרפון and רבי עקיבא argument in the קידש case. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says קידש is agreed by both, and the argument is only about בעל. That is why the גמרא says the משנה does not follow him.
steps.confusionAlert: Both rulings in this step sound like the משנה's rulings. The difference is the case: here they are said about בעל, not about קידש.

phrases.english: About what did they disagree? About one who had relations.
Rabbi Tarfon says:
He leaves the marriage contract payment among them and departs,
Rabbi Akiva says:
Not until he pays each and every one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא from step 7 by naming the case where they really argue.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the משנה does not follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר places the dispute in בעל, the very case the משנה left out

steps.title: The ברייתא finishes: buying is agreed, stealing is argued
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר adds a second pair. Everyone agrees that a buyer who does not know which of five sellers he bought from leaves the price among them. The argument is only about a thief who stole from one of five.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי טרפון and רבי עקיבא did not argue about a man who bought an item from one of five people and does not know which one he bought from. Everyone agrees he leaves the price among them and goes. They argued only about a man who stole from one of five. רבי טרפון says he leaves the stolen money among them and goes. רבי עקיבא says he is not free until he pays the stolen amount to each and every one of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from steps 7–8 keeps going. It now gives the money pair, matching the marriage pair: buying is agreed on, and stealing is where they argue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This mirrors step 7–8 exactly. קידש (betrothal) matches לקח (buying): no sin, so one payment is enough according to everyone. בעל (relations) matches גזל (stealing): there was wrongdoing, so רבי עקיבא demands that each person be paid.

keyTerms.meaning: bought an item
the price of the item
stole
the stolen item or money
leaves, walks away (and is free)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: קידש and לקח, everyone agrees on one payment. בעל and גזל, רבי עקיבא requires paying each one.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
phrases.english: Rabbi Tarfon and Rabbi Akiva did not disagree

phrases.aramaic: עַל שֶׁלָּקַח מִקָּח מֵחֲמִשָּׁה בְּנֵי אָדָם
phrases.english: about one who bought an item from one of five people
and he does not know which of them he bought from
that he leaves the price of the item among them and goes.
They disagreed only about one who stole from five,
for Rabbi Tarfon said:
He leaves the stolen amount among them and goes,
and Rabbi Akiva says:

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיְּשַׁלֵּם גְּזֵילָה לְכׇל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד.
phrases.english: Not until he pays the stolen amount to each and every one.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא עַל שֶׁלָּקַח מִקָּח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in steps 7–8 by adding the money cases.
steps.raayaObject: Shows which cases really are in dispute according to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר

steps.title: So the first opinion holds they argue about betrothal and buying: whose view is the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says there is no argument about קידש and לקח, the first opinion must hold that there is. So who wrote our משנה?
steps.simpleTranslation: Since רבי שמעון בן אלעזר said that they do not argue about 'betrothed' and 'bought,' we learn that the first opinion holds they do argue there. So whose view is the משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the ברייתא about the other opinion and then asks who the משנה follows. This sets up the problem spelled out in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר speaks as if he is correcting someone. That someone, the תנא קמא, must hold the argument is about קידש and לקח, while in בעל and גזל רבי טרפון agrees with רבי עקיבא. Now there are two clear opinions, and the משנה has to fit one of them.

keyTerms.meaning: by inference, we learn from this
the first opinion (the first, unnamed Sage)
they disagree
whose view is it?

steps.confusionAlert: The two opinions are mirror images. The first opinion says they argue about קידש and לקח. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says they argue about בעל and גזל.

phrases.english: Since Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said
that about 'betrothed' and 'bought' they do not disagree,
we learn that the first opinion holds they do disagree there.
Whose view is it?
phrases.notes: He means: whose view is our משנה?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּקָאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר בְּ״קִידֵּשׁ״ וְ״לָקַח״ לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the full ברייתא to work out the first opinion, then asks again who the משנה follows.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There are now two defined opinions, and the משנה's wording has to match one of them.

steps.title: The משנה's wording fits neither opinion
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה follows the first opinion, it should say קידש and לקח. If it follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, it should say בעל and גזל. It says קידש and גזל, which is a mix.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is the first opinion, the משנה should teach 'betrothed' and 'bought.' If it is רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, it should teach 'had relations' and 'stole.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the problem. The משנה pairs one case from each opinion, so it matches neither.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה puts the argument in קידש (the first opinion's case) and in גזל (רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's case). Each opinion explains only half of the משנה's wording. So we cannot tell whose view it is.

keyTerms.meaning: if
let it teach, it should have said
had relations (with her)

phrases.english: If it is the first opinion —
let it teach 'betrothed' and 'bought.'
If it is Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar —
let it teach 'had relations' and 'stole.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Lays out the question 'מני' in detail.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of the משנה (קידש and גזל)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה mixes one case from each opinion, so neither opinion can be its author.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: 'betrothed' means through relations
steps.stepSummary: The משנה really follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. The word קידש refers to a betrothal done through relations, and the משנה chose that word to show the strength of רבי עקיבא's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really it is רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. What does 'betrothed' mean? He betrothed her through relations. It taught 'betrothed' to show you how far רבי עקיבא's view goes,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. 'Betrothed' in the משנה is the same as his case of relations. The sentence continues in the next step, which explains רבי עקיבא's strength.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once קידש means 'betrothed through relations,' it matches רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's case of בעל, and גזל already matched. The משנה did not just say בעל because the word קידש makes רבי עקיבא's demand to pay every woman more striking. The גמרא is about to explain exactly why.

keyTerms.meaning: really, actually (keeping the original idea)
through relations (one of the ways to make קידושין)
to show you the strength (how far the view goes)

steps.confusionAlert: קידש בביאה is still a real קידושין. It is not just 'relations.' The משנה chose this wording on purpose.

phrases.english: Actually, it is Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar,
and what is 'betrothed'? He betrothed her through relations.
It taught 'betrothed,'
to show you the strength of Rabbi Akiva's view,

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר וּמַאי ״קִידֵּשׁ״ קִידֵּשׁ בְּבִיאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty about the משנה's wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting a word in the משנה (קידש means קידש בביאה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: קידש means an ordinary betrothal, so the משנה would fit neither opinion.
steps.terutzMaskana: קידש means a betrothal through relations, so the משנה fully matches רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. The wording was chosen to highlight רבי עקיבא's strength.

steps.title: Why the משנה chose the words קידש and גזל
steps.stepSummary: The משנה said קידש to show that רבי עקיבא fines a man even for breaking a rabbinic rule. It said גזל to show that רבי טרפון does not fine a man even for breaking a Torah rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: For even though he only broke a rabbinic prohibition, רבי עקיבא still fines him! And the משנה said 'stole' to show you how strong רבי טרפון's view is: even though the thief broke a Torah prohibition, רבי טרפון does not fine him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer from the last step. It explains why each word in the משנה shows the strength of one of the two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making קידושין through relations breaks only a rabbinic rule, yet רבי עקיבא still makes the man pay every woman. Stealing breaks a Torah rule, yet רבי טרפון still does not fine the thief. So the mixed wording is not a problem: each word picks the case where that opinion is most surprising.

keyTerms.meaning: A prohibition made by the Rabbis
A prohibition from the Torah itself
He fines or penalizes
His strength, meaning how far his opinion goes
He stole

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. It mixes קידש and גזל on purpose. קידש (a rabbinic violation) shows that רבי עקיבא fines even there. גזל (a Torah violation) shows that רבי טרפון does not fine even there.
steps.confusionAlert: Here קידש does not mean ordinary betrothal. As explained in the last step, it means a betrothal done through relations. That is why only a rabbinic rule was broken.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּאִיסּוּרָא דְּרַבָּנַן עֲבַד, קָנֵיס!
phrases.english: For even though he did something forbidden only by the Rabbis, he still fines him!
phrases.notes: This finishes the sentence from the last step. 'He' who fines is רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: And it taught 'stole,'
to show you how strong רבי טרפון's view is,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּאִיסּוּרָא דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא עֲבַד,
phrases.english: that even though he did something forbidden by the Torah,
he does not fine him.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּאִיסּוּרָא דְּרַבָּנַן עֲבַד, קָנֵיס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the תירוץ of step 12. It adds the reason for קידש and gives a matching reason for גזל.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each word is explained as chosen on purpose, to show the strength of a different opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The mix of קידש and גזל seemed to show that the משנה follows no single opinion
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. Each word highlights how far one opinion goes.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The wording question is fully settled.

steps.title: A woman returns from overseas: her son was with them
steps.stepSummary: She left with her husband and their son. If she says her husband died first, she is believed and is free of יבום. If she says her son died first, she is not believed for יבום, but she must do חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman went overseas with her husband, and her son was with them. She came back and said: 'My husband died, and afterward my son died.' She is believed. If she said: 'My son died, and afterward my husband died,' she is not believed. But we take her words into account, so she does חליצה and does not do יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. A woman who left with a child tells us the order of deaths, and the משנה rules when she is believed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When she left, she had a child, so she was free of יבום. If her husband died first, he left a son, and she stays free, which matches how she left, so she is believed. If her son died first, her husband died childless and she would need יבום. That would change her status, so she is not believed enough to do יבום. Still, we worry she may be right, so she needs חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Overseas, a faraway land
She is believed
We take her words into account and worry she may be right
She does חליצה, the ceremony that frees her from the יבם
She marries the יבם, her husband's brother

steps.confusionAlert: 'Not believed' does not mean we ignore her. We do not trust her enough to let her do יבום, but we trust her enough to require חליצה.

phrases.english: MISHNA: A woman who went, she and her husband,
overseas, and her son was with them,
and she came back and said:
'My husband died and afterward my son died'
she is believed.

phrases.aramaic: מֵת בְּנִי וְאַחַר כָּךְ מֵת בַּעְלִי״ —
phrases.english: If she said: 'My son died and afterward my husband died'
she is not believed.
But we take her words into account,
so she does חליצה and does not do יבום.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁהָלְכָה הִיא וּבַעְלָהּ לִמְדִינַת הַיָּם וּבְנָהּ עִמָּהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a brand-new משנה, unrelated to the earlier discussion about wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: She is believed when her claim keeps the status she left with (having a child). When her claim would require יבום, she is not believed for יבום but must do חליצה.

steps.title: She left childless and says a son was born overseas
steps.stepSummary: She left with no child. If she says the son died before her husband, she is believed and still needs יבום. If she says her husband died first, she is not believed to be free, so she does חליצה and not יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she said: 'A son was born to me overseas,' and said: 'My son died, and afterward my husband died,' she is believed. If she said: 'My husband died, and afterward my son died,' she is not believed. But we take her words into account, so she does חליצה and does not do יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the opposite case. This time the woman left with no children, and the rulings flip to match.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here she left childless, so she was someone who would need יבום. If the son died first, her husband still died childless, so nothing changes and she is believed, even for יבום. If her husband died first, she would be free of יבום. That changes her status, so she is not believed, but we still worry, so she does חליצה and not יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: A son was given to me, meaning a son was born to me
Afterward
My son
My husband

phrases.english: 'A son was born to me overseas,'

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרָה: ״מֵת בְּנִי, וְאַחַר כָּךְ מֵת בַּעְלִי״ —
phrases.english: and she said: 'My son died, and afterward my husband died'
she is believed.
If she said: 'My husband died, and afterward my son died'
she is not believed.
But we take her words into account,
so she does חליצה and does not do יבום.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The mirror image of step 14: she starts childless, so the believed and not-believed orders switch.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman who left childless is believed when her claim keeps her needing יבום. A claim that would free her is not accepted, so she does חליצה only.

steps.title: She says a יבם was born overseas
steps.stepSummary: Her husband had no brother when they left. She says a brother was born overseas, and then tells us either order of deaths. In both cases she is believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she said: 'A יבם was born for me overseas,' and said: 'My husband died and afterward my יבם died,' or 'My יבם died and afterward my husband died,' she is believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a third case: she claims a new brother-in-law was born while they were away. Whichever order of deaths she gives, she is believed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When she left, there was no brother at all, so she was never someone who needed יבום. The whole idea that a יבם exists comes only from her own words. So her story is accepted either way.

keyTerms.meaning: The husband's brother, who may do יבום or חליצה
My יבם
A יבם was born for me

steps.whatToRemember: The key to this משנה is how she left. She is believed when her story keeps that status. When her story would change it, she is not believed, but we still worry, so she does חליצה and not יבום. When the יבם himself is known only from her words, she is believed either way.

phrases.english: 'A יבם was born for me overseas,'
phrases.notes: She means a brother was born to her husband while they were away. When they left, he had none.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרָה: ״מֵת בַּעְלִי וְאַחַר כָּךְ מֵת יְבָמִי״,
phrases.english: and she said: 'My husband died and afterward my יבם died,'
or: 'My יבם died and afterward my husband died'
she is believed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third case. Instead of a son, it is a brother-in-law whose existence is known only from her own words.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the יבם was born overseas and is known only through her, she is believed whichever order of deaths she reports.

steps.title: She went with her husband and her יבם: not believed
steps.stepSummary: If she went overseas with both her husband and her יבם and comes back saying both died (in either order), she is not believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she, her husband, and her יבם all went overseas, and she comes back and says 'My husband died and then my יבם died' or 'My יבם died and then my husband died', she is not believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives its final case. Now she claims that both the husband and the יבם died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier cases her word was accepted at least partly. Here her claim also includes the death of the יבם, which would leave her free to marry anyone. The משנה says she is not believed about that, so she stays tied to the יבם.

keyTerms.meaning: The husband's brother, who may do יבום with the widow
Overseas, a far-away place
She is not believed

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with Step 16. There the husband had no brother when they left, and she said a brother was born overseas. Here the יבם was alive and went with them, and she says he died.

phrases.english: If she went, she and her husband and her יבם,
overseas, and she said:
"My husband died, and afterward my יבם",
or "My יבם, and afterward my husband" —
she is not believed,

steps.triggerLanguage: הָלְכָה הִיא וּבַעְלָהּ וִיבָמָהּ לִמְדִינַת הַיָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final case in the משנה's series of a woman reporting deaths overseas
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When she claims that both her husband and her יבם died, she is not believed in either order.

steps.title: The general rule: no one is believed to make himself or herself permitted this way
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives the reason with a list. A woman is not believed about her יבם or her sister dying, and a man is not believed about his brother or his wife dying, when the claim would permit a marriage for that person.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman is not believed to say 'my יבם died' so that she can marry someone else. She is not believed to say 'my sister died' so that she can marry her sister's husband. A man is not believed to say 'my brother died' so that he can do יבום with his brother's wife. He is not believed to say 'my wife died' so that he can marry her sister.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains the ruling of Step 17 with a general rule. It gives four parallel cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The special trust given to a woman who says 'my husband died' was made so she would not be left stuck as an עגונה. That trust does not reach other deaths that would only open a new marriage for the person speaking. In all four cases the speaker gains from the claim, so it is not accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: So that she may marry (someone else)
So that she may enter his house, meaning marry him
So that he may do יבום
A wife's sister, forbidden to him while the wife is alive

steps.whatToRemember: The trust given to a woman about her husband's death is a special rule. It does not cover other deaths that would permit a marriage: not the יבם, not a sister, not a brother, not a wife.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the limit of the special trust about a husband's death. It is a narrow exception and is not a general belief in anyone's report of a death.

phrases.english: because a woman is not believed to say
"My יבם died" so that she can marry,
and not "her sister died"
so that she can enter his house,
phrases.notes: "His house" means the sister's husband. While her sister is alive, she may not marry him.

phrases.english: and a man is not believed to say
"My brother died" so that he can do יבום with his wife,
and not "his wife died",
so that he can marry her sister.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for Step 17's ruling
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person is not believed to report a death when the report would permit a marriage for that same person (other than the special rule about a woman's own husband).

steps.title: Sending a גט through an agent when there is a יבם: benefit or harm?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רב נחמן: when a husband hands a גט to an agent for his wife and she has a יבם, does the גט count for her right away, even before it reaches her?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked רב נחמן: if a man gives a גט to someone to receive it for his wife, and she has a יבם, what is the law? Maybe since she dislikes the יבם, the גט is a benefit for her, and we may act for a person's benefit when they are not there. Or maybe since she sometimes likes him, the גט is a harm for her, and we may not act against a person when they are not there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a question. רבא wants to know if receiving a גט for a woman who has a יבם counts as doing her a favor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone may receive something for another person without asking only if it is a benefit for that person (זכין לאדם שלא בפניו). If the husband dies before the גט reaches her, the answer decides her status: is she divorced (and free of the יבם), or a widow who needs יבום? It depends on whether being free of the יבם is good or bad for her.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him (a question)
One who has a גט received on someone's behalf
We may act for a person's benefit even when he is not there
We may not act against a person's interest when he is not there
Perhaps

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רָבָא מֵרַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: גמרא: רבא asked רב נחמן:
One who gives a גט to be received for his wife
where there is a יבם, what is the law?
Since she hates him (the יבם) —
it is a benefit for her,
and we may act for a person's benefit when he is not there.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא: כֵּיוָן דְּזִימְנִין דְּרָחֲמָא לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: Or perhaps: since sometimes she loves him,
it is a harm for her,
and we may not act against a person when he is not there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins a new question, linked to the משנה's topic of the יבם
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a גט received for a woman who has a יבם counts as a benefit (so it takes effect right away) or a harm (so it does not take effect until it reaches her)

steps.title: רב נחמן answers from our משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן cites the משנה: 'We worry about her words, and she does חליצה and not יבום.' This shows that יבום is not clearly good or clearly bad for her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to him: we already learned it: 'We take her words seriously, and she does חליצה and not יבום.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers רבא from a line in our משנה. The line is about a woman whose report of the deaths is partly accepted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה takes her words seriously whether they would free her from the יבם or bind her to him. So the משנה does not treat being free of the יבם as a clear benefit for her. That means we cannot simply say the גט is a זכות for her.

keyTerms.meaning: We have learned it (in a משנה)
We take her words into account
She does חליצה, not יבום

phrases.english: He said to him: we learned it:
"And we take her words seriously,
phrases.notes: This is the line from our משנה that comes up in Steps 14 and 15.

phrases.english: and she does חליצה and not יבום."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's question in Step 19
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה treats her claims seriously in both directions. So freedom from the יבם is not a clear benefit, and the גט cannot simply be treated as a זכות for her.

steps.title: Sending a גט when the couple is fighting: benefit or harm?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רבא: if a husband sends a גט for his wife while they are quarreling, is the גט a benefit for her?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רבא: if a man gives a גט to be received for his wife while they are fighting, what is the law? Since she is fighting with him, maybe it is a benefit for her. Or maybe the comfort of being married matters more to her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a second, similar question. This time it is about a couple that is fighting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here there is no יבם. The question is only about the marriage itself. The fighting suggests she wants out, but she may still prefer the comfort and support of being married.

keyTerms.meaning: A quarrel or fight
Physical comfort, the ease of being married
Is preferable

phrases.english: רבינא said to רבא:
One who gives a גט to be received for his wife
where there is a quarrel, what is the law?
Since she has a quarrel with him —
it is a benefit for her.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִּלְמָא, נְיָחָא דְּגוּפָא עֲדִיף לַהּ?
phrases.english: Or perhaps the comfort of the body is preferable to her?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel question to Step 19, now about a fighting couple instead of a יבם
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a גט sent while the couple is quarreling counts as a benefit for the wife

steps.title: ריש לקיש: better to be married than alone
steps.stepSummary: The answer comes from ריש לקיש's saying that a woman prefers being with a husband over living alone. So even during a fight, the גט is not a clear benefit for her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: ריש לקיש said, 'It is better to sit as two than to sit as a widow.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבינא's question with a well-known saying quoted by ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The saying shows that a woman generally prefers being married, even with problems, over being alone. So a fight does not make the divorce a clear benefit for her. That means the גט cannot be received for her without her.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear, introducing a proof
It is better to sit as two
Being a widow, living alone

steps.whatToRemember: A גט is not treated as a clear benefit for a woman, whether she has a יבם or is fighting with her husband. Being married is generally seen as something she wants.
steps.whyThisMatters: This saying of ריש לקיש is quoted in many places in the גמרא as a general rule about what a woman prefers.

phrases.english: Come and hear, for ריש לקיש said:
It is better to sit as two
phrases.notes: "טן דו" means two bodies together, so she would rather live with a husband.

phrases.english: than to sit as a widow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's question in Step 21
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A woman prefers being married to being alone, so a גט sent during a quarrel is not a clear benefit for her.

steps.title: Three sayings: even a lowly husband is worth it to her
steps.stepSummary: אביי, רב פפא, and רב אשי each give a popular saying showing that a woman is proud to be married, even to a small, poor, or low-status man.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: A woman whose husband is as small as an ant still gets her seat placed among the noblewomen. רב פפא said: A woman whose husband is a wool comber calls him to sit with her at the doorway. רב אשי said: A woman whose husband sells cabbage heads does not even need lentils for her pot.
steps.whatsHappening: Three אמוראים add folk sayings that back up ריש לקיש's rule from the last step. Each one shows a woman proud to be married, even to a man of low standing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each saying uses a different kind of 'weak' husband: tiny, low-paid, or poor. In each case the wife still acts proud: she sits with important women, shows him off at the door, or does not mind going without food. This strengthens the point that a גט is not automatically a benefit for her, even when the couple is fighting.

keyTerms.meaning: A tiny ant-like creature. Here it means a very small, unimportant man.
Among the noblewomen, the free and important women
A wool comber, a lowly job
A seller of cabbage heads, a poor man
Lentils, the simplest food for the pot

phrases.english: Abaye said: one whose husband is as small as an ant,
her seat is placed among the noblewomen.
Rav Pappa said: one whose husband is a wool comber,
she calls him to the doorway of the house and sits with him.
Rav Ashi says: one whose husband sells cabbage heads,
does not need lentils for her pot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds popular sayings that support ריש לקיש's principle, which was used in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman values being married so much that even a small, poor, or low-status husband gives her pride and status.

steps.title: A teaching about some of these women
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא adds that all these women who seem so happy with their marriage are unfaithful and claim their children are their husbands'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: And all of them commit adultery and attribute the children to their husbands.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא adds a sharp comment on the women from the sayings just quoted. It gives one more reason why they are so eager to stay married.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Having a husband also gives them cover, because any child can be said to be his. This adds a second reason, beyond pride, why a married woman would not want to be divorced. So the main point stands: a גט is not a clear benefit for her.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught. This introduces a ברייתא, a teaching from the time of the משנה.
They commit adultery
They attribute, they hang it on someone

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a ruling about all married women. It is a comment on the women in the sayings just quoted, showing another reason they hold on to marriage.

phrases.english: It was taught: And all of them commit adultery
and attribute the children to their husbands.
phrases.notes: The word 'children' isn't written here, but the גמרא assumes it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comments on the women in the sayings from step 23 and adds another motive for staying married.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: These women also want a husband so they can claim any child is his.
steps.whatToRemember: This whole section supports ריש לקיש: a woman prefers being married. So a גט is not treated as a clear benefit for her, even during a quarrel. Because it is not clearly good for her, it cannot take effect for her before it reaches her hand.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter הָאִשָּׁה שָׁלוֹם
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula marking the end of the פרק הָאִשָּׁה שָׁלוֹם.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter הָאִשָּׁה שָׁלוֹם.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the traditional closing line said at the end of a פרק. It marks that the chapter הָאִשָּׁה שָׁלוֹם is finished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is not part of the argument. It is a farewell to the chapter and a promise to come back and learn it again.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you. This is the formula said at the end of a פרק.

phrases.english: We will return to you, chapter "The Woman, Peace"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the final discussion.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פרק הָאִשָּׁה שָׁלוֹם is completed.
